question: A sales manager wants to find out which sales reps logged the most calls this month. Which report type should they use?
explanation: The Tasks and Events report type shows calls, meetings, and tasks for users across the organization.
whyWrong: Activities with Accounts and Accounts with Activities focus on account-related activity, rather than calls and tasks across sales reps.
Activity History is a record page list, not a report type for building this report.

question: With standard field history tracking, how many fields can an administrator track per object?
explanation: Field history tracking supports up to 20 fields on each standard or custom object.
whyWrong: The limit is 20 fields per object, so 10, 15, and 25 are incorrect.

question: Which separate system permission is designed for transferring multiple records in bulk?
explanation: Transfer Records lets a user transfer records they do not own to other users.
whyWrong: View All gives read access to records; it does not grant permission to transfer them.
Modify All grants broad access and can also allow ownership changes, but Transfer Records is the separate permission designed for bulk transfers.
Edit lets a user change records they can access; it does not grant ownership-transfer rights for records they do not own.

question: A company wants an AI agent to answer common customer questions using approved company information and hand off complex cases to a person. Which Salesforce capability should the administrator configure?
options: Agentforce with an appropriate topic and actions
A scheduled Flow that runs once each day
A dashboard with a filtered report
A validation rule on the Case object
explanation: Agentforce can be configured with topics and actions for customer interactions, with appropriate controls and handoff for requests the agent cannot resolve.
whyWrong: A scheduled Flow runs at a defined time and is not a conversational agent for handling customer questions.
A dashboard presents report data; it does not respond to customer requests.
A validation rule checks data on save and cannot answer questions or route conversations.

question: Which record-triggered flow option runs before a record is saved?
explanation: A Before Save flow runs before Salesforce saves the record, so it can update field values or validate them.
whyWrong: A Platform Event flow starts from an event message; it is not a before-save timing option for a record-triggered flow.
An After Save flow runs after the record is saved, so it cannot change fields before that save.
An After Delete flow runs after a record is deleted; it does not run before a record is saved.

question: Which feature lets an admin change the components shown on a Home page?
explanation: Lightning App Builder lets admins customize a Home page by adding and arranging components.
whyWrong: Validation Rules check data entered in records; they do not change Home page components.
Record types control available picklist values and page layouts for records; they do not customize the Home page.
Profiles control access and settings. Lightning App Builder is used to arrange Home page components.
examDomain: Object Manager and Lightning App Builder

question: What can sales managers learn from a Campaign Influence report?
options: Campaigns that influenced opportunities and closed revenue
explanation: Campaign Influence reports show how marketing campaigns contributed to opportunities and closed revenue.
whyWrong: Email open rates are a separate marketing metric; they are not what Campaign Influence reports show in Sales Cloud.
Campaign Influence connects campaigns to opportunities and revenue; it is not limited to campaign spending.
Lead source counts do not show how campaigns influenced opportunity outcomes.

question: Which criteria options can a Case assignment rule use?
options: Both rule criteria and formula criteria
explanation: Case assignment rules can use field-based rule criteria or formula criteria.
whyWrong: Assignment rules can use formulas as well as field-based rule criteria.
Assignment rules can use field-based criteria as well as formulas.
Manual assignment is not a criteria type; it may be used when no rule assigns the case.

question: Why assign cases to a queue?
options: Give a team a shared list of cases to claim or work
explanation: A queue can own cases and give its members a shared list of work. Assignment rules or other routing tools can direct cases to the queue.
whyWrong: Queues are for routing and sharing work, not for creating reports.
Queues may send notifications, but their main purpose is to let a team work from a shared list of records.
Queues route and organize work; they do not delete cases.

question: Which records provide the product catalog and pricing that can be added to an opportunity?
explanation: Products define what a company sells, while price books and their entries define the prices available for opportunities.
whyWrong: Leads are part of the sales process, but they do not provide product and price book functionality on opportunities.
Campaigns track marketing activity; they are not needed to use products and price books with opportunities.
Opportunities are used in this process, but Products and Price Books provide the product data associated with them.

question: Which report format groups data by both rows and columns and shows subtotals where they meet?
explanation: Matrix reports group by rows and columns and show subtotals at their intersections.
whyWrong: Tabular reports are flat lists and do not show grouped subtotals.
Joined reports place multiple report types side by side; they do not create the row-and-column subtotal grid of a Matrix report.
Summary reports group rows and show subtotals for row groups, not at row-and-column intersections.
